t: You're on Wigmore Street, a busy West End street running about six hundred yards, parallel to and just north of Oxford Street, between Portman Square to the west and Cavendish Square to the east. The name comes from the village of Wigmore and its castle in Herefordshire, a seat of the family of Robert Harley, the politician from around the time of Queen Anne, who owned land in this area. Lewis de Teissier Prevost, a Royal Navy officer who lived from 1814 to 1907, was born on this street.
